gloss: Doing nothing is free. It is also the action an illegal submission is replaced by, so a price here would charge an agent for its own mistakes.
Arms every cell on a technique's row at once, which is why it costs twice what a form does.
Exactly what permitting costs. Vision pillar 1 rests on the permit/forbid decision being symmetric; any price difference turns denial from a peer strategy into a penalty.
A form's column is five cells against a technique's fourteen, and the price follows.
Symmetric with permitting a form, for the reason forbidding a technique is symmetric with permitting one.

One cell prised open against the ruleset, and one of a very small number of edict slots spent holding it there. It also costs essence: prising a cell open against your own ruleset is an enchantment on the world, and Vim is what an enchantment is made of. Untuned.
The same price as a dispensation, so that the surgical open and the surgical close are the same kind of decision.
Cheap, because the slot it frees is the scarce thing rather than the favor.

Per node tier — the resolved cost is this times the node's tier. Grants are restricted to prerequisite-free roots, so in v1 content the multiplier is almost always one; the scaling exists so that content with deeper roots does not make the summit cheap. It also costs vellum, because a founding grant is a text: the knowledge arrives in a mind by arriving first on a page somebody could have written.

A hundred and twenty months of raised research, teaching, and life. Priced to be a repeated decision rather than a once-a-run one. It also costs insight, which is what a blessing on a scholar is spent out of — the same stock her faculty teaches from, so a god who blesses constantly is a god whose university teaches slower.

Strictly the cheapest non-zero action, and deliberately so: it is the verb the god performs constantly, and a priced one would make most of the action space unaffordable no-ops, inflating illegalActionRate into noise.

Advancing an existing build. Founding a new one costs the separate `found-university-cost` constant, because §4.2 gives the two one action id and they are not the same purchase. It also costs stone, because raising a building should take stone and not only favour. Not labor: the world loop already spends that stock hiring the person-months, and charging it here too starved the verb.
Per cell, and it decays. The cheapest way to point a civilization at something, and the least durable.

Exceeds the favor cap at every worship tier below the highest, so the ruinous action is structurally unavailable to a young universe rather than merely expensive. It also zeroes whatever is left in the pool.

A raid is a tempo decision before it is a favor decision; the price is here so that it is also the second thing. It also costs passage, which is what holding a threshold open is made of — Limen, Fatum, Umbra. The dearest material price in the table, and the only one whose stock the v1 opening square produces on its own.
Free, and gated. Charging for the ending would make a god who spent well unable to stop.

Half again a portal, because an alliance opens the same threshold and then asks somebody to walk through it and stay. Untuned, and deliberately dearer than every intervention except changing tradition: a scholar of a species you cannot breed is the only way some civilizations grow a faculty at all.
